sections.heading: How to Redeem Build an Ant Empire Codes
paragraphs: You redeem codes in the game’s Settings interface. The upper-right Settings icon leads to the Codes tab, where you can enter the string and press Redeem. Copy and paste exactly as shown, including every letter and digit. Avoid adding a space before or after the code.

After submitting, read the response before trying again. A success message and an error message call for different next steps. This route does not require a separate redemption website. If you have not joined yet, use the official Roblox experience link and check that the developer is Insect Kingdom studio.

sections.heading: Why a Build an Ant Empire Code May Not Work
paragraphs: First compare the code against the active row. A recently replaced code can stop working even when an older guide still lists it. Next check the input: accidental spaces, missing digits and a mistyped letter are easy to overlook on a phone. Pasting directly avoids those manual typing errors.

If the game says the reward was already claimed, follow that account-specific message instead of repeatedly submitting the same string. If the interface seems stale after an update, rejoining is a reasonable general troubleshooting step, although it cannot make an expired code active. Note the exact error wording so you can distinguish an input problem from code availability.

sections.heading: Using a Cash Reward During Progression
paragraphs: Before redeeming a time-limited reward, it is practical to understand your next colony task. Know how to collect Food boxes, use the Sell station and choose a useful upgrade so you can spend your play session progressing rather than searching for basic controls. This is planning advice, not a promise of a fixed amount of Cash.

For a fresh colony, learn the production and selling loop first. Once that loop makes sense, compare Egg Luck, Egg Rolls, Food Value and additional colony space against your current needs. The code reward supports your session; it does not replace the ants and upgrades that drive ordinary progression.

description: See all Build an Ant Empire items with prices and effects, including Speed Jellies, Mutation Potions, and the Mutation Removal Potion.

hero.heading: Build an Ant Empire Items
hero.lead: The item reference lists 11 items: 4 Speed Jellies, 6 mutation-applying potions and 1 Mutation Removal Potion. The Items Shop is at the center of the map, according to the September 30 guide.

sections.heading: All Build an Ant Empire Items, Prices and Effects
paragraphs: Use this table to compare the listed Cash price and effect before buying. Speed Jellies describe movement speed and a timed duration; mutation-applying potions describe an EFF multiplier. Mutation Removal Potion has a separate purpose: it removes an ant’s mutation rather than adding another multiplier.

Prices below preserve the September 30, 2026 item guide’s notation. Check the current shop before confirming a purchase after an update. The difference between an inexpensive temporary item and a late-progression potion is substantial, so read the entire price suffix instead of comparing only the leading number.

sections.heading: Speed Jellies
paragraphs: All four listed Speed Jellies provide temporary movement speed. Their duration is part of the effect, so a higher multiplier should be considered alongside the time it lasts and the Cash it costs. They are consumable items, not permanent upgrades to the whole colony. Plan to use a timed item when you intend to keep playing and observe its effect.

subsections.heading: Normal Speed Jelly
paragraphs: Normal costs $10k and gives 1.3x movement speed for 5 minutes. It is the cheapest listed item. A low shop price does not automatically make it your best next purchase if you still need Cash for a core colony upgrade.

subsections.heading: Strong Speed Jelly
paragraphs: Strong costs $100M and gives 1.6x movement speed for 10 minutes. Compare that cost against your present wallet and next upgrade, rather than treating it as a small step up from Normal just because both are jellies.

subsections.heading: Super Speed Jelly
paragraphs: Super costs $10T and gives 2x movement speed for 15 minutes. The listed effect is movement speed; do not substitute a production multiplier or an extra reward for the effect actually shown.

subsections.heading: Prismatic Speed Jelly
paragraphs: Prismatic costs $100Qa and gives 2.5x movement speed for 15 minutes. It has the largest listed Speed Jelly multiplier, but its temporary duration still matters when you decide whether it fits your current session.

sections.heading: Mutation Potions
paragraphs: Leaf, Bubblegum, Candy, Rainbow, Petal and Starlight apply their named mutations. Their listed EFF multipliers range from 1.35x for Leaf to 5x for Starlight. This makes the potion table useful for comparing effects, but it does not establish which ant you should always target or how a second mutation application behaves.

Consider a potion for an ant you expect to keep using. An expensive item is a deliberate single-ant purchase, while colony upgrades serve different progression needs. Review the intended target and current confirmation text before consuming anything, especially when the potion represents a large share of your wallet.

links.label: Compare mutation potions
links.description: See all six EFF multipliers, their prices and the separate removal option.

sections.heading: Mutation Removal Potion
paragraphs: Mutation Removal Potion costs $100k and removes an ant’s mutation. It is neither a Speed Jelly nor a way to grant one of the six listed positive multipliers. Check which ant is selected and what mutation it currently has before using the item.

The listed effect is removal. Do not budget around receiving the original potion’s price back, and do not assume a removed mutation can be restored without another application. Treat the purchase as its own decision. If your goal is simply faster movement for a limited session, compare the timed jellies instead of buying a removal item.

sections.heading: How to Buy and Use Items
paragraphs: Look for the Items Shop at the center of the map, as described in the item guide. Compare the item name, Cash price and effect, then buy the item you intend to use. Use it on the chosen ant through the current game interface and read any selection or confirmation before committing.

Items are consumed on use. That makes target selection and timing more important than they would be for a permanent menu setting. For a timed jelly, consider whether you can use the listed duration. For a mutation potion, think about whether the selected ant is likely to remain part of your colony. Exact menu presentation can change; the visible item description should guide the final purchase.

sections.heading: Which Items Should Beginners Buy First?
paragraphs: Begin by establishing a stable Food-to-Cash loop and useful upgrades. Even the cheapest listed item competes with other early spending, and the larger potion prices belong to very different wallet sizes. There is no single item purchase that every new player must make before understanding the Ant Queen, slots and selling.

If your immediate problem is limited colony space, extra room addresses that problem more directly than an unrelated consumable. If you are comparing permanent progression with a short timed effect, consider what you can still use when the duration ends. Keep a reserve for your next useful ant or upgrade instead of spending every available unit of Cash in the shop.

hero.heading: Build an Ant Empire Beginner Guide
hero.lead: First run: Ant Queen → roll/buy an ant → place it in a colony slot → collect Food boxes → sell for Cash → buy useful upgrades → repeat.

sections.heading: Build an Ant Empire Core Loop
paragraphs: Build an Ant Empire starts with a small colony and asks you to grow it by rolling ants, collecting Food, earning Cash and upgrading. The Ant Queen is your starting point for rolling or buying ants and eggs. Ants belong in colony slots, where they help generate the Food boxes that you sell for Cash.

Think of this as a repeating production loop. An ant alone is not the whole route: you also need to place it, collect what it produces and sell that output. Reinvesting the resulting Cash opens up further colony progress. Before looking for an advanced strategy, complete the whole cycle once so you can tell which step is slowing you down.

sections.heading: Your First 10 Minutes
paragraphs: Use this sequence as a first-session checklist, not a promise of a certain Cash total after ten minutes. How quickly you progress depends on your play and the current game. On keyboard, WASD moves, Space jumps and E interacts. Pay attention to the interaction shown by the game when you approach a usable object.

You begin with one colony slot. More slots cost more as you expand, so do not assume you can immediately place every ant you roll. Check your available space before spending heavily at the Ant Queen. A worker and a free slot need to come together for the production loop to grow.

sections.heading: Best Early Upgrades
paragraphs: The September 30 beginner guide recommends Egg Luck and Egg Rolls early. Egg Luck improves the odds of better ants, while Egg Rolls gives more rolls at the Ant Queen. They address different parts of the same recruitment task. This is a practical starting recommendation, rather than a fixed order announced by the developer for every possible colony.

Next compare Food Value and Colony Expansion. Food Value raises what each box sells for; Colony Expansion adds room and slots. If you lack space for ants, expansion answers that need. If your existing boxes need to earn more, look at value. Ant Speed is another category and makes ants produce food faster. Choose according to the constraint you actually see.

sections.heading: When to Buy Items and Mutations
paragraphs: Items are secondary purchases to consider alongside your core colony. The item reference starts at Normal Speed Jelly for $10k, but mutation-applying potions range from Leaf at $1M to Starlight at $5.1Qi. That range is a useful reminder that shop items are not all intended for the same wallet.

A Speed Jelly gives timed movement speed. A mutation potion applies a named EFF multiplier to an ant. Neither should be confused with buying another colony slot. Since consumables are used up, choose an ant you expect to keep before spending on an expensive potion. If a purchase empties your balance and delays your next necessary upgrade, waiting may be more practical.

sections.heading: Pets and Auto Jelly Feed
paragraphs: The new Pet System connects Dungeon activity to pet coins and pet egg hatching. Its route is Dungeon → collect pet coins → hatch a pet egg. When you explore it, use the requirement shown by the current egg interface instead of planning around an old fixed price or a guessed list of pets.

Auto Jelly Feed is a separate feature that automatically feeds ants with jelly. It can reduce manual feeding actions when you use that system, but it does not replace the basic Cash loop. Neither feature needs to be treated as a compulsory first-minute task. Learn your colony first, then inspect the live interfaces when you are ready to explore more systems.

sections.heading: Beginner Mistakes to Avoid
paragraphs: Do not spend all your Cash before deciding what the colony needs next. A purchase can be useful in isolation but still delay the slot, ant or upgrade that would help you right now. Keep your next goal visible and reconsider it after each collection-and-sale cycle.

Avoid using an expensive potion on an ant you are about to replace. Do not confuse an inactive code with the active entry. Check the developer and game name when following a guide: Ants Empire and Build An Ant Empire are different experiences. Finally, compare real effects rather than copying an exact level or price table from another game. Your current shop and upgrade interface should determine the final confirmation.

faq.question: How do you play Build an Ant Empire?
faq.answer: Roll or buy ants at the Ant Queen, place them in colony slots, collect Food boxes, sell for Cash and reinvest in useful upgrades. Repeat this cycle as your colony expands.

faq.question: What controls does the game use?
faq.answer: The keyboard controls in the beginner guide are WASD for movement, Space for jumping and E for interaction. Follow current on-screen controls for your device.

faq.question: What should I upgrade first?
faq.answer: Egg Luck and Egg Rolls are the beginner reference’s early recommendations. Then compare Food Value and Colony Expansion according to your current needs, with Ant Speed for faster production.

faq.question: How do I earn Cash?
faq.answer: Collect Food boxes produced by your ants and use the Sell station. Food Value upgrades raise the sale value of those boxes.

faq.question: How do I get more ants?
faq.answer: Use the Ant Queen to roll or buy ants and eggs. Check colony space so you can place the ants you intend to use.

faq.question: Should beginners buy Mutation Potions immediately?
faq.answer: Start by understanding the Cash loop and core upgrades. Expensive potions make more sense when you can afford them and have an ant you intend to keep.

hero.lead: To get pets, collect pet coins in the Dungeon and use them to hatch a pet egg. Check the current egg interface for the requirement before you hatch.

sections.heading: How to Get Pets in Build an Ant Empire
paragraphs: The Pet System update describes a simple route: collect pet coins in the Dungeon, then hatch a pet egg. This links the activity, currency and hatching step in one progression task. If you came here looking for pets, start with that route rather than using your ordinary ant-rolling instructions at the Ant Queen.

Open the current game and inspect its Dungeon and pet interfaces. Read any displayed access or hatching requirement before spending time collecting toward a target. Treat the live interface as your checklist: it tells you what you can do now and what it still asks for. The steps below keep the route practical without assigning a fixed coin yield or an egg price.

sections.heading: How Pet Coins and the Dungeon Connect
paragraphs: Pet coins are the currency named in the update’s pet-hatching route, and the Dungeon is where the update says to collect them. Keep that relationship separate from the colony’s Food-to-Cash loop. Selling Food gives Cash for colony progress; the pet route specifically calls for pet coins collected through Dungeon content.

When planning a session, check which goal you are pursuing. If the egg asks for pet coins, ordinary Cash should not be assumed to satisfy that requirement. Read the currency label beside the amount and compare it with the balance shown in the current pet system. A number without its currency label is not enough to tell whether you are ready to hatch.

sections.heading: Pet Eggs
paragraphs: Pet eggs are the hatching step at the end of the described route. Before pressing the hatch control, check the live requirement, the currency label and any information the interface provides about the egg. If an update changes the requirement, the game’s current display is more useful than a saved screenshot of an older value.

Use any pet names, collection information or odds shown by the current egg interface to guide your decision. Do not plan around a guessed roster or assume that a picture from another game represents an available hatch here. If a detail is not displayed, focus on the actions you can see: collecting the requested currency, meeting the shown requirement and checking the hatch result.

sections.heading: What the Update Confirmed
paragraphs: The Pet System announcement connects pet egg hatching with collecting pet coins in the Dungeon. That is the key addition for a player trying to understand where pets come from. It gives you a task route rather than a complete catalogue of pet stats, costs and probabilities.

The same update snapshot also mentions Auto Jelly Feed, which automatically feeds ants with jelly. These are separate systems: one describes pet acquisition, and the other describes feeding convenience. Seeing both in an update does not mean that enabling automatic feeding grants pet coins or hatches an egg. Use each interface for the task it names.

sections.heading: Pet System Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If you cannot see pet coins, first make sure you are inspecting the current Dungeon and pet systems. Look for a currency label and any relevant on-screen requirement. Do not assume that your Cash balance is the pet-coin balance. If you are looking at colony upgrades, return to the system associated with pets before deciding that coins are missing.

If the egg button is locked, read the message beside it. Compare the displayed requirement with your current balance and any other condition the game lists. Avoid copying a fixed egg cost from an old comment and treating it as the only possible explanation for a locked button.

If your interface differs from a recent update description, rejoining a current server is a reasonable general check. It is not a guarantee that an access condition will disappear. After rejoining, inspect the interface again and follow the current message. Keep track of which control you used and what response it gave, so you can distinguish an access issue from a hatching requirement.

paragraphs: Pets are a useful separate goal to explore once the ordinary colony route makes sense to you. Keep the Ant Queen, colony slots, Food collection and selling cycle clear in your mind before switching tasks. This helps you recognize which interface and currency belong to the goal you are pursuing.

There is no need to turn the pet route into a race against an invented timetable. Check your current objective, inspect the Dungeon access and work toward the requirement the game actually displays. If your immediate colony problem is space or Food sale value, address that through colony upgrades and return to pet hatching when it fits your session.

hero.heading: Build an Ant Empire Auto Jelly Feed Guide
hero.lead: Auto Jelly Feed is a new feature that automatically feeds ants with jelly. Open the current feeding controls, enable the option shown by the game and observe an eligible feeding action.

sections.heading: What Auto Jelly Feed Does
paragraphs: Auto Jelly Feed automatically feeds ants with jelly. The feature’s purpose is feeding convenience: it can reduce the manual feeding actions you need to perform while using that system. Keep that straightforward purpose in mind when deciding whether to turn it on during your session.

Automatic feeding does not by itself explain which input the current game accepts, whether a target must be selected, or what conditions a feeding action requires. Read those details from the live controls before enabling the feature. The useful first question is whether the interface is ready for an eligible feed, rather than whether enough seconds have passed according to a guessed timer.

sections.heading: How to Use Auto Jelly Feed
paragraphs: Start in the live game and open the current ant or jelly feeding controls. Look for the Auto Jelly Feed option displayed by the current build. If the interface asks you to select an ant or target, do that before expecting the next feeding action. If it does not show a target selector, do not search for a menu from an unrelated guide.

Read any input requirement and confirm the feature’s enabled state. Then observe the next eligible feeding action. Use what the game shows to decide whether it is operating as intended. Watching an action after enabling it is more informative than repeatedly switching settings without checking the result.

steps.heading: Open the current feeding controls
steps.description: Inspect the live ant or jelly feeding interface.

steps.heading: Confirm a target if shown
steps.description: Choose an ant or feeding target only when the current interface requires one.

steps.heading: Enable Auto Jelly Feed

steps.heading: Observe an eligible feeding action

sections.heading: What to Check If Auto Jelly Feed Is Not Working
paragraphs: Check the feature state first. An available setting is not necessarily an enabled setting, so inspect the current indicator instead of assuming a prior click activated it. Read any message shown by the interface. If it explains a requirement, address that requirement before changing unrelated colony upgrades.

Next inspect the jelly or input that the feeding controls show as available. A shop item with the word jelly in its name should not be assumed to satisfy this interface. Compare the input label here with the resource or item the game asks you to provide. If a selection is required, check the chosen ant and any eligibility message beside it.

If your controls look different after an update, rejoining a current server is a reasonable general step. It cannot guarantee a feed when the game’s current conditions are not met. Change one thing at a time and observe the result so you can tell whether the issue was the setting, the displayed input or the selected target.

subsections.heading: A practical feeding checklist
bullets: Confirm that the automatic feeding option is enabled.
Check the input shown by the current feeding interface.
Inspect the target only if the game requires a selection.
Read any eligibility or requirement message.
Consider current server state when the interface appears stale.

sections.heading: Auto Jelly Feed vs Speed Jellies
paragraphs: Auto Jelly Feed describes an action: feeding ants automatically. Speed Jellies in the item reference describe consumable effects: temporary movement speed for a listed duration. These descriptions answer different questions. Do not assume that buying a Speed Jelly automatically supplies the input expected by the feeding feature.

For example, Normal Speed Jelly is listed at $10k for 1.3x movement speed over 5 minutes. That item information does not tell you the automatic feeder’s accepted inputs, feeding interval or target rules. Check the feeding interface for those controls and use the item table when you want to compare the shop’s speed effects. Shared wording is not enough to establish shared resource behavior.

sections.heading: When to Use It in Your Progression
paragraphs: Use automatic feeding when feeding convenience would help your current session and the live interface shows that you can use it. It is a way to manage repeated manual actions, rather than a substitute for the ordinary progression route. You still grow the colony through ants, Food, Cash and useful upgrades.

A new player benefits from learning the basic route before configuring additional systems. Once you understand what you are doing manually, an automatic option is easier to assess: you can observe whether it performs the intended action and check the current requirements. Avoid buying unrelated items simply because you hope they will unlock a setting the game has not asked you to buy.

faq.question: What is Auto Jelly Feed?
faq.answer: It is a feature that automatically feeds ants with jelly. Its stated benefit is automating the feeding action.

faq.question: Is Auto Jelly Feed new?
faq.answer: It appears as an addition in the current New Update event snapshot, alongside the separate Pet System.

faq.question: Where do I turn it on?
faq.answer: Open the current ant or jelly feeding controls and use the Auto Jelly Feed option shown by the live game. Menu presentation can change after updates.

faq.question: Why is Auto Jelly Feed not feeding an ant?
faq.answer: Check its enabled state, the input shown as available and any target or eligibility requirement the interface displays. Read the game’s message before retrying.

faq.question: Is Auto Jelly Feed the same as using a Speed Jelly?
faq.answer: Treat them separately. Auto Jelly Feed automates feeding; listed Speed Jellies provide timed movement-speed effects. Use the live feeding controls to identify their accepted input.

title: Build an Ant Empire Mutations | Potions & Multipliers
description: See every Build an Ant Empire mutation, potion price, EFF multiplier, removal option, and practical tips for choosing which ants to mutate.
searchIntent: See every Build an Ant Empire mutation, potion price, EFF multiplier, removal option, and practical tips for choosing which ants to mutate.

hero.heading: Build an Ant Empire Mutations
hero.lead: Six mutations are listed: Leaf 1.35x, Bubblegum 1.75x, Candy 2x, Rainbow 2.25x, Petal 3x and Starlight 5x EFF. Mutation Removal Potion costs $100k and removes an ant’s mutation.

sections.heading: All Build an Ant Empire Mutations
paragraphs: Compare potion prices and EFF multipliers in the table below. Each row identifies one named mutation and the consumable that applies it. Starlight has the largest listed multiplier at 5x, while Leaf has the lowest listed application cost at $1M. A larger multiplier and a suitable purchase for your current wallet are different decisions.

The price range spans several stages of spending. Read the full suffix in the cost column before choosing a potion, and check the live shop before confirming a purchase after an update. This table follows the September 30 item reference. It is a comparison of listed effects, not an official ranking of ants or a promise of a fixed Cash return.

sections.heading: How Mutation Potions Work
paragraphs: A mutation potion applies its named mutation to a chosen ant and gives the EFF multiplier listed for that mutation. Select the intended ant through the current item interface and review the item’s description before use. The potion is consumed, so a careful target check matters when the purchase represents a large part of your wallet.

For example, Leaf is listed as 1.35x EFF and Bubblegum as 1.75x EFF. Keep the effect label intact when comparing them. EFF is the label used by the item reference; it should not be silently replaced by an invented movement-speed percentage or a guaranteed earnings formula. If you want temporary movement speed, that is a separate shop-item category.

sections.heading: Mutation Removal Potion
paragraphs: Mutation Removal Potion costs $100k and removes an ant’s mutation. It belongs beside this list because it changes the mutation state, but it does not apply Leaf, Bubblegum or any other listed positive multiplier. Check the selected ant’s current mutation before deciding that removal is the action you want.

Do not assume that removal refunds the original application cost. The stated item effect is removing the mutation. If you plan to apply another potion afterward, treat that as a separate consumable decision and read the game’s current behavior before using it. A removal item is useful for understanding the available option, not a reason to ignore target selection on the original purchase.

sections.heading: Which Mutation Should You Use?
paragraphs: Start with budget and target choice. An expensive potion is easier to justify on an ant you intend to keep than on one you expect to replace soon. That is a practical spending principle rather than an official tier list. Check what else your colony needs before committing a large amount of Cash to one ant.

Leaf and Bubblegum have different listed prices and multipliers, as do the higher-cost options. Compare the improvement you are considering against the next useful colony purchase. A larger EFF number does not mean you should empty your wallet for it immediately. If you need more slots to use your ants, expansion addresses a different problem that a potion cannot be assumed to solve.

For the highest listed effect, Starlight gives 5x EFF at $5.1Qi. For a lower-cost entry point to the listed mutations, Leaf gives 1.35x at $1M. These comparisons help you read the table; they do not establish a fixed purchase order for every colony. Let your current wallet and the ant you plan to keep determine which option is practical.

links.label: Compare colony spending first
links.description: See whether Food Value, colony space or another core upgrade addresses your immediate bottleneck.

sections.heading: Do Mutations Stack?
paragraphs: Before applying a second mutation potion to the same ant, read the current selection and confirmation text. The item reference explains application and removal, but it does not supply a stacking rule that you should use for budget calculations. In particular, do not multiply two listed EFF values together and assume that the result will be your ant’s final effect.

Inspect the ant’s current mutation state and the action the live interface describes. If the confirmation does not clearly explain what happens to the existing mutation, pause before consuming another expensive potion. You can still choose a first mutation from the table without building a strategy around an assumed combination.

sections.heading: Mutations vs Speed Jellies
paragraphs: Mutation potions and Speed Jellies solve different item tasks. The item guide describes mutations as lasting until removal, while Speed Jellies have explicit temporary durations. A mutation carries the listed EFF effect; a Speed Jelly describes movement speed for 5, 10 or 15 minutes depending on the item.

This difference matters when planning a play session. A timed effect should be considered with the period in which you intend to use it. A mutation should be considered with the ant you intend to keep using. Neither description supplies a complete rule for every interaction between systems, so use the current game display before assuming one item automatically changes another feature.

faq.answer: The listed mutations are Leaf, Bubblegum, Candy, Rainbow, Petal and Starlight. Their potion prices and EFF multipliers appear in the table.

faq.question: What is the strongest listed mutation multiplier?
faq.answer: Starlight has the highest listed multiplier at 5x EFF. That comparison concerns the item effect, not a full ranking of ants or a guaranteed Cash return.

faq.question: How much is Starlight Mutation Potion?
faq.answer: The September 30 item reference lists Starlight Mutation Potion at $5.1Qi. Read the current shop price before confirming a purchase.

faq.answer: It costs $100k and removes an ant’s mutation. Do not assume it refunds the cost of the potion that applied the mutation.

faq.question: Are mutations permanent?
faq.answer: The item guide describes mutations as lasting until removal, unlike timed Speed Jellies. Mutation Removal Potion is the listed way to remove a mutation.

title: Build an Ant Empire Upgrades | Best Upgrade Order
description: Use this Build an Ant Empire upgrades guide to prioritize Egg Luck, Egg Rolls, Food Value, colony expansion, ant speed, and early Cash spending.
searchIntent: Use this Build an Ant Empire upgrades guide to prioritize Egg Luck, Egg Rolls, Food Value, colony expansion, ant speed, and early Cash spending.

hero.heading: Build an Ant Empire Upgrades
hero.lead: Practical early order: Egg Luck → Egg Rolls → Food Value or Colony Expansion for your current bottleneck → Ant Speed when production speed limits you. This is a beginner-guide recommendation, not an official fixed meta.

sections.heading: All Build an Ant Empire Upgrade Types
paragraphs: The beginner reference identifies five upgrade categories. Each changes a different part of your colony’s progression, so begin by matching an effect to the task that is slowing you down. More room helps with slots; more value helps what boxes sell for; faster production helps the rate at which ants produce Food.

Egg Luck and Egg Rolls relate to the Ant Queen rather than the selling step. Read the current upgrade menu for prices and available purchases, especially after an update. The category table below is an effect reference. It deliberately does not turn one guide’s general recommendation into a fixed price or level schedule for every stage of play.

table.caption: Colony upgrade categories
rows: Adds more room and slots for ants
Raises how much each box sells for
Gives more rolls at the Ant Queen

sections.heading: Best Early Upgrade Order
paragraphs: The September 30 beginner guide recommends prioritizing Egg Luck and Egg Rolls early, then Food Value and colony expansion. Use that as a practical starting point. Egg Luck improves the odds of better ants, and Egg Rolls gives more rolls at the Ant Queen, so these choices support recruitment before you reassess how the colony uses its workers.

After that, inspect your bottleneck. If you have ants to use but not enough room, Colony Expansion addresses space and slots. If your current boxes need to earn more, Food Value improves sale value. If production speed is the limiting factor, Ant Speed makes ants produce food faster. This condition-based choice is more useful than buying an upgrade only because it occupies the next line in a rigid list.

Check what the next useful purchase costs in the live menu and keep enough Cash to make progress toward it. You do not need an invented exact level target to make a good decision. Observe one collection-and-sale cycle after a purchase and reconsider what would help next.

sections.heading: Egg Luck vs Egg Rolls
paragraphs: Egg Luck and Egg Rolls support the same recruitment activity in different ways. Luck improves the odds of better ants. Rolls gives more rolls at the Ant Queen. More attempts and better odds are not interchangeable effects, so compare the labels carefully rather than treating both as a single generic ant upgrade.

A practical early approach is to consider both while building your starting colony. Read the current menu and balance purchases against your available Cash. Do not assign a guessed percentage to Egg Luck or promise a named ant after a specific number of rolls. The effect descriptions explain why the categories matter without establishing a guaranteed outcome.

Before more recruitment spending, also check your colony slots. An ant you cannot currently place may not address the immediate production problem. If space is your constraint, return to the expansion decision rather than continuing to buy recruitment improvements by habit.

sections.heading: Food Value vs Colony Expansion
paragraphs: Food Value raises how much each box sells for. Colony Expansion adds room and slots for ants. The distinction is straightforward: one changes the sale-value part of the loop, and the other changes the space available to the workforce. Your current colony determines which of those constraints is more pressing.

If the colony has usable space but each sale feels small relative to your next goal, inspect Food Value. If you want to place more ants and the slots are full, inspect expansion. More slots cost more as you grow, so use the price shown in the current interface instead of assuming every new slot costs the same.

sections.heading: When Ant Speed Matters
paragraphs: Ant Speed makes ants produce food faster. Consider it when production speed is the step limiting your current loop. First make sure you are collecting and selling the Food you already have, since a purchase should be matched to the step that actually needs improvement.

Keep Ant Speed separate from the movement-speed effect of a shop Speed Jelly. The upgrade reference describes faster Food production; the jelly reference describes temporary movement speed with a listed duration. They should not be treated as identical merely because both use the word speed. Compare the permanent progression category and the consumable item using their own descriptions.

sections.heading: Upgrades vs Items and Mutations
paragraphs: Colony upgrades belong to your core progression decisions. Items add another set of purchases, including temporary Speed Jellies, mutation-applying potions and Mutation Removal Potion. A potion changes a chosen ant’s mutation, while colony expansion adds room and slots. Buying one is not the same as buying the other.

Before an expensive potion, decide whether the ant is one you intend to keep and whether the colony still has a more immediate upgrade need. The listed item prices span from $10k for Normal Speed Jelly to $5.1Qi for Starlight Mutation Potion. That range reinforces why you should compare purchases against your current wallet instead of copying a late-game shopping list into a new colony.

links.label: Compare shop purchases
links.description: Read prices, timed effects and consumable usage before spending.

links.label: Read mutation choices
links.description: Compare EFF potions and the removal option separately from core upgrades.

sections.heading: Upgrade Mistakes to Avoid
paragraphs: Avoid copying a fixed price or level table from another ant game. Check that the game is Build An Ant Empire by Insect Kingdom studio and read the present upgrade interface. A similar name is not enough to make another game’s progression data relevant here.

Do not spend every unit of Cash without checking the next useful purchase. Do not buy extra recruitment improvements without looking at available slots. Finally, do not treat a mutation potion as a colony expansion upgrade. Each purchase has a job; make that job clear before confirming and review your needs again as the colony grows.

links.description: Follow rolling, placement, Food collection and selling as one complete loop.

faq.question: What should I upgrade first?
faq.answer: The current beginner reference recommends Egg Luck and Egg Rolls early. Then compare Food Value and Colony Expansion according to your current bottleneck, with Ant Speed when production speed limits you.

faq.question: What does Egg Luck do?
faq.answer: It improves the odds of better ants. Read the live menu for the current purchase options rather than assuming a fixed percentage.

faq.question: What do Egg Rolls do?
faq.answer: Egg Rolls gives more rolls at the Ant Queen. It changes the available rolling opportunities, while Egg Luck affects the odds of better ants.

faq.question: What does Food Value do?
faq.answer: It raises the sale value of Food boxes, improving the value side of the collect-and-sell loop.

faq.question: What does Colony Expansion do?
faq.answer: It adds more room and slots for ants. Consider it when you need space for the workers you want to place.

faq.question: What does Ant Speed do?
faq.answer: It makes ants produce food faster. Keep this upgrade effect separate from the temporary movement speed of a shop Speed Jelly.

faq.question: Should I buy upgrades or Mutation Potions first?
faq.answer: Compare the colony’s immediate need with the cost of the potion. For early progression, establishing the loop and useful core upgrades is a practical priority; expensive potions suit an ant you intend to keep.
